author: Sample commentary (synthetic data)
headline: Real spending rose 21% since FY2016 while population fell 5%: 28% more per resident, and 68% of measures met their FY2025 target.
paragraphs: In FY2025 dollars, city departments spent 21% more than in FY2016. Population fell, so spending per resident rose faster. Both numbers are real, and neither says whether the money bought better outcomes; that is the job of the measures views.

Departments met 68% of the measures they reported in FY2025. That number is only as honest as the measures: 13 measures were dropped over the decade and targets were made easier 247 times, 134 of them the year after a miss. The integrity view lists each.
Overtime was $471 million in FY2025, 48% of it in public-safety departments where minimum staffing rules drive it.

caveats.text: Actuals include pass-through and one-time federal funds; the FY2021–22 spike is mostly not local money.
Performance measures are self-reported by departments; the Controller audits only a sample.
